title: YOLOv3 Forward-Direction Person Signal Analysis — Comprehensive Summary

methodology.description: Paired image comparison: identical scene with human present vs human absent. Forward pass through YOLOv3 capturing all conv layer feature maps. Delta = features(with_human) - features(without_human). This delta IS the person signal inside the network.

saliency_results.interpretation: Model strongly detects person (score=1.01) when present, near-zero (0.016) when absent. Saliency maps show which input pixels drive the detection — these are the regions an adversarial patch should target or be near.

layer_rankings.interpretation: Layer 54 is the single most person-sensitive layer. A 56% relative change means the channel activations change by more than half their baseline magnitude when a person is present. Channels 479, 31, 51 are the most person-tuned individual channels in the network.

frequency_analysis.method: FFT applied to delta (with-without) feature maps, not raw images and not reconstructions. This measures what frequencies the human signal has AFTER network processing.
frequency_analysis.key_finding: The human signal undergoes a FREQUENCY CASCADE through the network depth. It is NOT a single frequency — it shifts from LF-dominant at early layers to MF-dominant at deep layers, then back to LF at detection heads.

cascade_pattern.interpretation: Person is a large low-frequency blob at full resolution
Network begins encoding person structure — edges, limbs, boundaries add mid and high frequency content
Mid-frequency content reaches maximum. Person structure is encoded as medium-scale patterns at 26x26 resolution
At 13x13 feature maps, the person is a high-frequency event relative to the small grid. Most balanced spectrum — broadband disruption needed here
Network has made its decision. Person signal collapses to low-frequency yes/no at anchor prediction level

polynomial_fft.method: Each channel's spatial activation treated as polynomial coefficients. FFT of these coefficients reveals the polynomial degree spectrum of the embedding.
polynomial_fft.finding: Dominant polynomial degrees are at DC (degree 0) and Nyquist (degree N-1), with harmonics at degrees 1, 2, 3. This means the model represents the person as a combination of very low-degree (smooth, global) and very high-degree (rapidly varying, local) polynomial features.
polynomial_fft.symmetry_note: Polynomial FFT appears symmetric because input coefficients are real-valued. For real input X, |X[k]| = |X[N-k]| by conjugate symmetry. Only bins 0 to N/2 carry unique information.

1d_delta_fft_oscillation.cause: The oscillation in the 1D delta FFT plot is NOT signal oscillation — it is visual redundancy from plotting both halves of a real-valued FFT. Bins 0 to N/2 are unique; bins N/2 to N mirror them.
1d_delta_fft_oscillation.top_frequencies: Dominant 1D frequency is consistently at bin = feature_map_width (one full cycle across the map). The person creates one major spatial event spanning the feature map — the fundamental harmonic.

layer_54.notes: HIGHEST PERSON SENSITIVITY. MF peaks here at 26.3%. Largest HF delta (+0.008). This is the optimal layer to target with adversarial patches.

layer_60.notes: Most balanced LF/MF/HF at 26x26 resolution. Near-equal three-band split.

layer_62.notes: MF DOMINANT layer. 1024 channels at 13x13. Most broadband person signal. Patch targeting this layer needs LF+MF+HF content.

layer_63.notes: HIGHEST MAX RELATIVE DELTA in network (2.548). MF dominant. Channel 422 appears in both person-sensitivity and spectral power rankings.

layer_75.notes: 2nd most person-sensitive. Channel 170 appears here and at detection heads — likely a person-anchor channel.

layer_81.notes: Detection head (13x13 scale). 255 channels = 3 anchors x 85 (5+80 classes). Low relative delta — decision already made.

layer_93.notes: Detection head (26x26 scale). Channels 170, 171 appear as top person channels — these are likely person-class anchor outputs.

layer_105.notes: Detection head (52x52 scale). Highest absolute delta but lowest relative. Near-pure LF. Channels 170, 171 again dominant.

channel_170.role: Person anchor channel — appears across all detection scales as top person-sensitive channel

channel_171.role: Person anchor channel at medium and fine scales

channel_422.role: Deep person feature — appears in both backbone and detection-adjacent layers

channel_47.role: Consistent person feature across deep layers

channel_51.role: Appears at both early and deep layers — person edge detector

primary_target.frequency_content_needed: Mid-frequency dominant (MF=26.3%). Patch should contain medium-scale patterns that map to ~1/4 to 1/2 the feature map Nyquist frequency. At 416px input and 26x26 feature map, each feature cell covers ~16 input pixels. Mid-frequency patterns at this scale correspond to ~8-16 pixel features in the patch.
primary_target.expected_impact: 56% relative activation change — highest in network

secondary_target.frequency_content_needed: Broadband (LF=26%, MF=43%, HF=32%). Patch needs large smooth gradients PLUS medium detail PLUS fine high-frequency content.
secondary_target.expected_impact: Max single-channel relative delta = 2.548 (highest in network)

tertiary_target.frequency_content_needed: MF dominant (41%) with significant HF (25%). Medium-to-fine patterns.
tertiary_target.expected_impact: 50% relative delta. Channel 170 is a cross-scale person anchor.

detection_head_disruption.strategy: Target channels 170 and 171 which appear consistently across all detection scales. These are likely the person-class anchor output channels. Disrupting them directly attacks the detection decision.
detection_head_disruption.frequency: LF dominant — large smooth patches are sufficient at detection heads

adversarial_patch_implications.frequency_cascade_summary: A patch designed for early layers should be smooth and low-frequency. A patch for mid layers (37-60) should have medium-scale structure. A patch for deep layers (62-75) should be broadband with fine detail. A multi-scale patch that contains all frequency bands will disrupt the person signal at every depth.

scripts.frequency_analysis: freq_analysis.py — delta FFT + polynomial FFT + 2D FFT
